When they "cancel out" all background noise. It's good in some situations, but sometimes it detracts from the atmosphere around whatever is going on, whether it be someone speaking into a mic or a video recording of something happening.

Echos and a dull roar in the background, for example, add to the atmosphere of what was really going on in the situation. especially if watching that video far from when it was recorded.
You know what I don't like about some microphones?

I use a dynamic mic for recording, which is supposed to pick up less background noise than a condenser mic. Even so, I can still hear the heater in the room turn on and off in the background during playback, which I really don't like. What kind of recording do you do and why do you want background noise?

I'm saying that not filtering the background noise allows you to, you know, pick up all the sound in the area. It just makes sense to me to capture everything sometimes.

And yes, I understand the premise of filtering background noise.
